Abstract—Finding high-performing formulations is difficult
when few have been measured and experimental budgets are
limited. We propose KolTa, an active learning framework that
selects batches to discover the top 5% of formulations at a target
temperature under a fixed query budget. KolTa combines a three-
stage predictor of component contributions, role-conditioned in-
teractions, and anchored temperature response with task-specific
soft physics constraints. Its Physics-Residual-Calibrated Upper
Confidence Bound (PRC-UCB) acquisition rule combines pre-
dicted utility, ensemble disagreement, and a target-temperature
physics residual, with nonnegative exploration weights fitted to
out-of-fold signed errors. We evaluate the framework on three
measured tasks and one simulated task covering binary-mixture
viscosity, drug solubility, ionic-liquid viscosity, and electrolyte
conductivity. KolTa ranks first or second in mean area under
the learning curve (AULC) on every task and outperforms seven
of the eight comparator strategies in paired tests, winning 75
of 78 paired comparisons across tasks and seeds against those
seven strategies. Across the three measured tasks, its largest gap
to the best mean AULC is 0.032, compared with at least 0.056 for
every comparator. On Drug, reaching 80% average recovery of
the remaining targets across drugs requires an estimated median
of 348 additional formulation queries, about 18% fewer than
the fastest comparator. Researchers can adapt the framework
to diverse formulation problems through component roles and
physical constraints.

Impact Statement—Developing multi-component formulations
such as drug–solvent systems, ionic-liquid mixtures, and battery
electrolytes requires screening large candidate spaces under tight
experimental budgets. KolTa helps formulation teams prioritize
which candidates to prepare and measure next by combining
multi-temperature records with component roles and governing
temperature relations. Across four campaigns spanning viscosity,
solubility, and conductivity, the framework consistently ranks in
the top two discovery strategies without retuning its acquisition
rule for each domain, cutting median additional queries to
recover 80% of the remaining top-5% drug–solvent systems
by nearly one-fifth relative to the fastest baseline. Practitioners
can adapt its role-conditioned interactions and soft physical
constraints to accelerate early-stage laboratory screening.

Goal-directed molecular generation requires
satisfying heterogeneous constraints such
as protein–ligand compatibility and multi-
objective drug-like properties, yet existing
methods often optimize these constraints in
isolation, failing to reconcile conflicting ob-
jectives (e.g., affinity vs. safety), and strug-
gle to navigate the non-differentiable chem-
ical space without compromising structural
validity. To address these challenges, we
propose CAGenMol, a condition-aware dis-
crete diffusion framework over molecular se-
quences that formulates molecular design as
conditional denoising guided by heterogeneous
structural and property signals. By coupling
discrete diffusion with reinforcement learn-
ing, the model aligns the generation trajec-
tory with non-differentiable objectives while
preserving chemical validity and diversity.
The non-autoregressive nature of diffusion
language model further enables iterative re-
finement of molecular fragments at inference
time. Experiments on structure-conditioned,
property-conditioned, and dual-conditioned
benchmarks demonstrate consistent improve-
ments over state-of-the-art methods in bind-
ing affinity, drug-likeness, and success rate,
highlighting the effectiveness of our frame-
work. The code is available at https://
github.com/Lee612-1/CAGenMol.
